result: In 415 tertiary-referral CFS patients mean PSQI was 10.17 and ESS 10.51, with no linear ESS-PSQI relation and an insomnia-like subgroup (n=69, ESS<5, PSQI 11.51).
reason: Subjective questionnaires only, no controls; finding is about objective PSG measures and no atlas finding covers subjective sleep scores

result: In 25 young CFS/POTS vs 20 controls on incremental tilt, absolute CBFV was slightly lower, neuronally activated CBFV averaged 0 and fell with angle, n-back performance worsened with orthostasis, and critical closing pressure was raised.
reason: Same measure (TCD CBFV on tilt) but absolute fall only slight; main contribution is neurovascular uncoupling and cognitive decline with tilt, so extends rather than replicates

result: In 25 young CFS/POTS vs 20 controls on incremental tilt, absolute CBFV was slightly lower, activated CBFV was abolished and fell with angle, working memory deteriorated with orthostasis, and CCP was raised.
reason: TCD velocity not volume flow, only slight absolute reduction; adds neurovascular coupling and cognition, so extends

result: 3T VBM in 26 CFS vs 26 matched controls reported significant regional grey and white matter volume changes (regions truncated in abstract), interpreted as linked to memory, visual processing and motor planning.
reason: Positive regional volume finding runs against the claim of no consistent structural abnormality; small single-group study, abstract truncated

result: Echocardiography showed smaller LV end-diastolic and end-systolic dimensions, stroke volume index, cardiac index and LV mass index in 26 CFS with OI than in 20 CFS without OI and 27 controls.
reason: Same measure (LV size, stroke volume) in ME/CFS, same direction; earlier Miwa paper than the cited 2026 one

result: No XMRV/MLV nucleic acids, infectious virus or antibodies were found in 58 Canadian CFS patients or 57 controls using nested PCR, qRT-PCR, culture and immunoblot.
reason: Independent negative cohort consistent with the refuted XMRV finding

result: In 67 women with CFS vs sedentary controls over 6 days of accelerometry, patients were less active and more sedentary, and higher activity correlated with more symptoms and variability the same and next day (r 0.24-0.42).
reason: Does not test whether deconditioning explains abnormalities; activity-to-next-day-symptom correlation bears on delayed PEM, though cross-sectional

result: Three RT-qPCRs found no XMRV/HMRV/MLV group G3 in white cells of 78 Swedish ME/CFS (30 with FM) and 7 FM patients or 168 blood donor sera, with controls for mouse DNA contamination.
reason: Independent negative cohort consistent with the refuted XMRV finding

result: In 107 ME/CFS, 37 chronic fatigue and 20 controls, IL-1, TNF-alpha, neopterin, lysozyme and PMN-elastase were higher in ME/CFS, and IL-1/TNF correlated with fatigue and flu-like malaise.
reason: Raised TNF matches the meta-analytic direction; only 20 controls
